title: Hatimoğulları: Alevis should play an active role in the peace process
content:
DEM Party Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları called on the Alevi community to actively participate in the peace and democratization process in Turkey. At a meeting with representatives of Alevi organizations in Istanbul, she criticized the exclusion of Alevis from parliamentary deliberations and warned against leaving the future of the process solely in the hands of the government. Lasting peace, she argued, could only be achieved on the basis of equal citizenship, legally guaranteed fundamental freedoms, and the democratic restructuring of the republic.




The meeting took place at the Kazım Karabekir Cemevi in Istanbul’s Ümraniye district. Alongside representatives of Alevi associations and institutions, numerous other guests attended the event. Speaking here, Hatimoğulları emphasized that the process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan must not be understood as a power struggle between political camps. “We do not view peace in terms of one side winning and the other losing. Peace means building a shared life and giving one another our consent to do so. Genuine peace can only emerge when all 86 million citizens of this country can live in justice, freedom, and peace.”




Criticism of the exclusion of the Alevi community

title: Iranian security bodies block medical leave for Kurdish political prisoner
content:
Iranian security bodies have blocked medical leave and access to adequate treatment for Fahim Ebadi, a Kurdish political prisoner in Orumiyeh Central Prison who suffers from diabetes, high blood pressure and high blood fat levels, the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported.




Iranian forces arrested Ebadi, who is from Orumiyeh and is serving a 45-month sentence, in the city around two years ago.




After several weeks of interrogation at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, he was transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison, where he has remained since.




After several months in detention, a branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Court of Orumiyeh sentenced him to 60 months in prison on charges of “membership of opposition groups” in connection with membership of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).




His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months after he waived his right to appeal and requested a sentence reduction.

title: Resistance against solar power plant project in Kulp on day 91
content:
Resistance against the planned solar power plant project.in the village of Cixsê, in the Kulp district of Amed (Diyarbakır), has continued for three months. For 91 days, residents have maintained a vigil in protest against the project, which threatens grazing lands, water sources, and agricultural livelihoods. An investigation by the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) has now confirmed significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment. The organization is calling for the immediate cancellation of the project.




Representatives of the TMMOB Coordination Council in Amed presented their findings during a protest in Cixsê. The findings are based on a site inspection conducted on October 14, during which experts examined both the proposed construction site and the information contained in the environmental impact assessment documentation.




Grazing lands and water sources at risk




According to Filiz Kaçar, a member of TMMOB’s Energy and Ecology Commission, approximately 30 hectares of land within and around the project area are used as grazing grounds for livestock. The installation of solar panels, fencing of the site, and construction of access roads would fragment continuous grazing areas and significantly restrict their use. title: Concern for at Least 14 Kurdish prisoners facing death sentences in Iran
content:
30 October has been declared International Day of Political Prisoners. A review of published human rights reports identifies at least 14 Kurdish political prisoners and protesters facing death sentences in Iran.




This list brings together reported cases and includes both initial court rulings and sentences upheld on appeal. Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir, Yousef Ahmadi, Pezhman Touberehrizi, Arman Marefati, Mohammad Faraji, Raouf Sheikh-Maroufi and Mohsen Eslamkhah are eight of these prisoners.




Earlier human rights reports warned that they could face execution. The reports described unfair and secretive proceedings, torture, pressure to obtain forced confessions, and violations of their right to defend themselves.




Hatem Ozdemir is a Kurdish citizen of Turkey imprisoned in Iran. Khosrow Mohammadnia, Masoud Toushmalani, Sirwan Shabani, Borzou Rezaei and Omran Amani are five others on the list. They were sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests. The sentences against the first three were reported on 1 October, and Rezaei’s on 6 October. On 29 October, it was reported that 21-year-old Omran Amani had been formally informed of his death sentence at Great Tehran Penitentiary.

author: Unknown
title: Human rights violations against Kurds continue in Iran
content:
The Iranian regime’s practices of detention, imprisonment and punishment targeting Kurds continue. According to information reported by the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), a request for medical leave by Fehîm Ebadî, a Kurdish prisoner with diabetes held in Urmia Central Prison, has been rejected, preventing him from accessing medical treatment.




Ebadî was detained by Iranian regime forces in Urmia two years ago. He was sentenced to five years in prison on the allegation of being a “member of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).” His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months.




Detained without a warrant




Mohammad Reza, who lives in the Malekshahi region of Ilam Province, was detained by Iranian regime forces and taken to an undisclosed location. According to KHRN, Mohammad Reza was detained at his family home in the early hours of the morning on 29 October, without the authorities presenting an arrest warrant. No information has yet emerged regarding the grounds for his detention.




Kurdish cultural activist arrested




Metîn Feremerzpûr, a Kurdish cultural activist and doctoral student in philosophy at the University of Tabriz, was also detained by regime forces on allegations of “propaganda against the state” and taken to Mahabad Prison. author: Unknown
title: DEM Party delegation meets with prisoners: Rights violations continue in Aegean region
content:
A DEM Party delegation which included MPs Nevroz Uysal Aslan, Burcugül Çubuk, İbrahim Akın, Vezir Parlak, and Onur Düşünmez, met with prisoners held at Buca and Aliağa Şakran prisons between 26 and 29 October.




Speaking outside Şakran Prison, lawyer and MP Nevroz Uysal Aslan said prisoners’ access to social activities was being restricted, problems were occurring during conditional release procedures, and petitions were being left unanswered.




Aslan noted that some women prisoners at Şakran were being prevented from using the shared exercise yard, that the imposition of identity requirements continued, and that some detainees were being denied access to their rights to sports, outdoor exercise, and social activities.




She also stated that sick prisoners were facing obstacles in accessing healthcare, while letters, books, and publications in Kurdish were being delayed or withheld.




Referring also to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Nevroz Uysal Aslan said political prisoners held in prisons should be released to pave the way for democratic politics and enable legal steps to be taken.




The delegation’s prison visits are expected to continue at Bodrum S-Type Prison.

title: Kobanê students: Our language is our existence
content:
Students in Kobanê protested against the Syrian Ministry of Education's decision to limit Kurdish-language education to three lessons. The students said that Kurdish was a fundamental part of their identity and existence and expressed their desire to continue receiving education in their mother tongue. 




We want to continue receiving education in our mother tongue




Eleventh-grade student Rehef Feysel Sedûn told ANF that they were not opposed to any language and that every people had the right to receive education in their mother tongue. Rehef Feysel Sedûn said, "I am the daughter of Martyr Abu Layla, and I have been receiving education in my own language for 11 years. We want to continue receiving education in our mother tongue. We already have Arabic and English lessons as well."







 







Rehef Feysel Sedûn pointed out that millions of Kurds had the right to receive education in their own language, stressing that mother-tongue education was a fundamental right of every people.




Rehef Feysel Sedûn, who wants to become a lawyer, said, "As Kurds, we also have the right to receive education in our mother tongue. I want to become a lawyer, and my dream was to do so in my own language. I want to fulfil my dreams in my mother tongue and defend my people in my own language."

content:

As part of the international campaign “Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, a Political Solution to the Kurdish Question,” a letter has been sent to the Presidency of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe (CoE). According to information provided by the campaign organisers, the letter was prepared with the support of 620 signatories from 29 countries around the world.




The letter, sent ahead of the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers' human rights meeting, scheduled to take place from 1 to 3 December 2026, calls for the implementation of the 2014 ruling by the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) concerning Öcalan.




According to information shared by the campaign organisers, the new letter has received the support of 58 elected representatives. The signing initiative also includes individuals affiliated with 30 political parties, 90 civil society organisations and 16 trade unions.

title: Attacker who shot Rojda Odabaşı cites ‘noise’ as motive
content:
Rojda Odabaşı, who was seriously wounded when Mazlum Çelebi shot her with a shotgun on the night of 23 August in Diyarbakır (Amed), continues her fight for justice. Odabaşı is still receiving treatment for injuries sustained in the armed attack by Çelebi, reportedly her downstairs neighbour. However, the attacker, who was arrested on the day of the incident, was released after 58 days in detention. Reacting to the release of Çelebi, who was indicted on charges of "intentional injury" and "damage to property", Odabaşı asked, "Did I have to die for him to be punished?"




First hearing scheduled for 8 April 2027




Mazlum Çelebi, who shot and wounded Rojda Odabaşı and damaged her vehicle, was detained on 23 August and remanded in custody the same day. The indictment prepared in connection with the incident seeks his punishment on charges of "intentional injury" and "damage to property". Çelebi reportedly justified the attack in his statement by saying, "They were making noise."




Following the preparation of the indictment, the court ordered Çelebi's release in a preliminary procedural decision issued on 23 October. Odabaşı subsequently requested a restraining order and protective measures, stating that her personal safety was at risk. The first hearing in the case is scheduled for 8 April 2027 at Diyarbakır 2nd Criminal Court of First Instance.

title: Kurdish businessman arrested in Belgium
content:
Businessman Muhsin Talay, who sought refuge in Belgium, has been arrested in Brussels on the basis of an Interpol notice issued at Turkey’s request. Talay, who was acquitted in a murder trial before a court in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), is now in custody. His asylum proceedings in Belgium are still pending. His family warns of possible extradition to Turkey and calls on the Belgian authorities to grant him protection.




Murder accusation despite court acquittal




The arrest is linked to the murder of Murat Baycan, who was killed under unclear circumstances in Amed in 2005. Baycan is alleged to have worked as an informant and agent for the Turkish intelligence service (MIT). Muhsin Talay was accused of involvement in the killing but was acquitted in the subsequent proceedings before the 4th High Criminal Court in Amed.




According to his family, Talay continues to be linked to the murder despite his acquittal. The allegations are reportedly based on a report by the Turkish intelligence service (MIT), even though the evidence presented during the trial was discredited. The family accuses the Turkish authorities of seeking to prosecute and sentence Talay again on this basis.




Talay was reportedly subjected to repeated pressure from MIT during the court proceedings. Fearing mistreatment and renewed prosecution, he eventually left Turkey and applied for asylum in Belgium.

title: YJK-E and KON-MED launch campaign against femicide and patriarchal violence
content:
The Kurdish Women’s Association in Germany (YJK-E) and the Confederation of Kurdistan Communities in Germany (KON-MED) are launching a nationwide campaign against femicide, patriarchal violence, and the structural oppression of women on November 1. Under the slogan “We are intensifying our social struggle against femicide and patriarchal mindsets,” seminars, educational programs, and public events are planned through International Women’s Day on March 8. The campaign will focus on developing democratic family structures, promoting gender equality, and protecting women’s lives.




In their joint statement, the two umbrella organizations criticize the fact that women are subjected to violence in all areas of life, even in a country like Germany, which professes a commitment to fundamental democratic values and human rights. According to the organizations, a total of 105 women have been killed since the beginning of 2026, with Kurdish women accounting for approximately ten percent of the victims. “These women are not just numbers. Each of them had a life, dreams, a family, children, and a future that was taken away from her,” the statement reads.




Patriarchal violence does not begin with femicide

title: Iranian regime sentences Van resident Cenk Demir to 5 years in prison
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) stated that a regime court in the city of Urmia had sentenced Cenk Demir, originally from Van (Wan), to five years in prison on charges of “membership in opposition groups.”




According to the statement, Demir was arrested in Urmia approximately eight months ago. After being questioned for months at a security detention centre in the city, he was transferred to Urmia Central Prison.




It was reported that, following the announcement of the verdict, Demir was transferred to the Ershad ward, where political prisoners are held.

title: The Kurdistan Region’s experience of government – I
content:
The Kurdistan Region is facing the consequences of its failure to form a government on every front, as the balance of power in the Middle East is once again being tested and the region faces the prospect of major changes. Two political forces remain determined to secure their respective demands in the government formation process: the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) and the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). In this series, we look back at the history of government formation in the Kurdistan Region, beginning with its first government.




The Kurdistan Front after the Raperin uprising




Following the First Gulf War and the Raperin (uprising) of March 1991, the Iraqi government withdrew its administrative institutions from much of the region in October 1991, following United Nations Resolution 688 and the establishment of a no-fly zone north of the 36th parallel by the allied powers. The administrative vacuum left by the withdrawal was filled by the Kurdistan Front (Bereya Kurdistanê), marking the beginning of a period of de facto autonomy for the Kurds.




The Front was established in 1987–1988 by the KDP, PUK, the Kurdistan Democratic People's Party (KPDP) and the Kurdistan Socialist Party-PASOK (Kurdistan Democratic Independence Party). By 1992, it had developed into an eight-party umbrella organisation with the participation of the Iraqi Communist Party, the Kurdistan

title: Karayılan commemorates fallen guerrillas from Shengal
content:
Murat Karayılan, a member of the Central Headquarters of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG), has issued a statement commemorating seven fallen Kurdish guerrilla fighters from Shengal. He paid tribute to their contribution to defending the Yazidi population against the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) and to establishing independent self-defense structures in Shengal. Karayılan also commented on the talks between the Iraqi government and the leadership of the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ). He welcomed the prospect of integrating the YBŞ into the Iraqi army, provided that the units retain their local character and remain permanently responsible for protecting the population.




In his statement, Karayılan recalled the genocide perpetrated by ISIS against the Yazidis in August 2014, which the Yazidi community refers to as the 74th Ferman, as well as the role of the Kurdish guerrillas in defending Shengal. He regards the YBŞ and YJŞ forces established during that period as a crucial achievement in the struggle to prevent another genocide.

title: Bar associations file criminal complaint against deforestation in Gabar and Besta
content:
The bar associations of Siirt and Şırnak have filed criminal complaints over the ongoing deforestation in the Gabar and Besta regions. They are demanding an immediate halt to the tree felling and criminal investigations into those responsible. The complaints target both individuals involved in the deforestation and public officials suspected of bearing responsibility.




According to the environmental and urban development commissions of both bar associations, the relevant complaints were submitted to the public prosecutors’ offices in Siirt and Şırnak. They concern tree felling carried out between April 20 and July 29, 2025, which reportedly continued beyond that period.




The lawyers are calling for investigations into suspected illegal tree felling, the unlawful transportation of timber and other forest products, and possible complicity in these activities. They are demanding that prosecutors identify those responsible, initiate criminal proceedings, and order examinations of the affected logging and storage sites to secure evidence.




At the same time, the bar associations are demanding full disclosure of the official permits and environmental decisions authorizing the logging operations. author: Unknown
title: Kurdish protester wounded by IRGC sentenced to prison and fined
content:
Milad Ebrahimi, a 31-year-old Kurdish man from Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province, who was shot and wounded by Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces during the December 2025–January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to one year in prison and fined four billion rials on charges of “disturbing public order”.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Branch 101 of the Kamyaran Criminal Court Two tried Ebrahimi in mid-October. He was notified of the verdict on 25 October.




IRGC forces shot Ebrahimi in the lower back with live ammunition during protests in Kamyaran on the evening of 8 January 2026.




He was taken to a medical facility in Sanandaj, the provincial capital, where he underwent surgery before returning home to recover.




Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested him on 1 February, despite his need for further hospitalisation because of an infection caused by his gunshot wound, and took him to the ministry’s detention facility in Sanandaj.




He was denied access to a lawyer and medical care during his detention and was provisionally released on bail on 27 February.

content:

Ruçem Vefa Elyakut, co-chair of the DBP’s provincial branch in Amed, praised the local community’s struggle. “The people of Arzoxlî have been putting up dignified resistance for days,” she said. Today, it wants to plunder this land using the same methods. We will never accept that.”




Construction work resumes despite ongoing court proceedings




At the center of the dispute is the “ZENKAR-2 Solar Power Plant and Energy Storage Facility” project developed by the company Zenkar. title: Environmentalists demand projects in Zîlan Valley to be halted immediately’
content:

Reading the statement, Rojhat Özgökçe, a representative of the Mesopotamia Ecology Movement, said the works threatened agricultural land, water resources, and biodiversity.




Özgökçe said that disrupting the natural flow of the Zîlan Stream could have irreversible consequences for the Erciş Plain, the Çelebibağ Wetlands, and the habitats of endemic species.

content:

The complaint called for investigations to be opened and criminal proceedings to be brought against the relevant public officials and those carrying out the felling, over allegations of unlawful tree cutting, the transportation of illegally obtained forest products, and aiding these activities. The statement emphasised that the bar associations would continue to defend forests, wildlife, and citizens’ right to live in a healthy environment.

title: DEM Party: The Republic must be updated
content:
The Turkish Republic was officially proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the country's new capital. In a statement titled “May the Republic endure, democracy prevail, and the brotherhood of peoples remain eternal in the second century,” the co-chairs of the DEM Party, Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan marked the 103rd anniversary saying that citizenship could only be fully realised through an understanding that guarantees equal protection for everyone’s language, identity, culture, beliefs and opinions. The statement emphasised that Turks, Kurds and other peoples, together with all religious communities, are equal owners of the country.




The message added: “A democratic future can only be built through a shared life in which we all have an equal voice and an equal say in decision-making. A Türkiye in which women live as equals, workers enjoy security, young people have hope, and the law applies equally to everyone is possible. A Democratic Republic is one in which no one is required to be like anyone else and the will of the people is respected. This is also a vision of a country where people can live together in greater peace and harmony. An independent judiciary, the rule of law, universal human rights, a free press, the separation of powers and strong local democracy are essential to achieving this.”

He argued that the struggle against corruption could not be separated from the struggle for democracy, as the weakening of oversight mechanisms and the suppression of public dissent had facilitated the plundering of public resources.




‘The state aims to dismantle the Freedom Movement’

title: YJA Star guerrillas: We gained our identity as resisting women through Bêrîtan
content:
Commander Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş) was commemorated by her comrades in the guerrilla areas on the 34th anniversary of her martyrdom. Commander Bêrîtan was martyred in 1992 after carrying out a self-sacrificial action in Xakurkê during the war against the Turkish state and its collaborators. Bêrîtan, who became a symbol of women who refused to submit in the face of calls for surrender, established a new path of struggle. Guerrillas of the Free Women's Units (YJA Star) shared their feelings and thoughts on the anniversary of Martyr Bêrîtan's death.




YJA Star guerrilla Avaşîn Efrîn

 







 







"First of all, on the anniversary of Comrade Bêrîtan's martyrdom, we respectfully commemorate all the martyrs of freedom. We have reached this stage thanks to the efforts and truth of our pioneering martyrs. We will never forget the efforts of these heroes. Through her stance, Comrade Bêrîtan showed us the path of self-sacrifice. Bêrîtan's path is the path of freedom, and it is also the path of all martyrs. We unite around this path and educate ourselves on this basis. Particularly in this period, establishing genuine comradeship with Abdullah Öcalan is possible through a proper understanding of the martyrs. Thanks to Comrade Bêrîtan, we learned how to struggle as YJA Star guerrillas, came to know ourselves and developed an identity. On this basis, we renew our promise to uphold th

author: Unknown
title: Shengal is at a historic turning point
content:
Shengal is now at a historic turning point. Shengal’s existence and integration bring with them a comprehensive unity with Iraq. The integration of the collective will and the genuine integration of people’s everyday lives represent the first concrete step towards bringing the two communities together in a shared life, while preserving their mother tongues and native cultures. The political reality and future represent a historic stage in which this social unity is translated into a political reality.




The coming together of the two communities through their respective cultural values and their ability to live in their mother tongues forms the cornerstone of this process. This political and cultural integration carries a force that connects with the reality of Abdullah Öcalan’s life and unites the entire society around this collective will.




This historic process expresses the will of the people of Shengal to determine their own future and live on an equal footing with Iraqi society, while also laying the foundations for building a shared future, peace and stability.




A shared political future aims to strengthen the political and social status of the Shengal region within Iraq as a whole and to permanently enshrine the people’s right to self-determination on a constitutional basis.

author: Unknown
title: Iran sentences three protest detainees to death, whereabouts unknown
content:
Branch 23 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran has sentenced three men arrested during the December 2025–January 2026 protests to death on charges of “espionage.”




An informed source who spoke to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) said that the men, named Mehdi, Amir-Reza and Vahid, were notified of their sentences in Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary on 26 October.




The source added that on 28 October, the three political prisoners were summoned to the prison’s guard office on the pretext of being transferred to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, but were taken to an undisclosed location.




Security forces arrested the three men during the protests in Tehran and transferred them to the Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary after a period in detention. Their case was referred to Branch 23 following their indictment on charges of “espionage”, the source said.




At the time of the report, their transfer to Ghezel Hesar Prison remained unconfirmed, with no precise information available about the trial proceedings or the latest status of their cases.

title: Kurdish Peace Mothers to launch a vigil in Ankara
content:
The Peace Mothers Initiative aims to increase pressure for concrete steps in the peace and democratic society process through a multi-day vigil in the Turkish capital, Ankara. Representatives of the Peace Mothers’ Councils from 24 cities will gather on November 1, hold talks with political parties, and set up a protest tent. Their central demands include freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, action to address the situation of political prisoners, and accountability from the Turkish state for advancing the peace process.




At a press conference held at the branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) in the province of Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), Nezahat Teke recalled that Öcalan’s call on February 27, 2025, had raised great hopes. “However, for these hopes to develop into a genuine peace process, the state must also take action. If Öcalan is not free, any laws that are passed will be meaningless,” Teke said.




Demands for Öcalan’s freedom and improved prison conditions




The Peace Mothers are demanding that Öcalan be granted a legally and politically recognized status that would enable him to participate actively in the peace process. According to Teke, his inclusion in existing or planned commissions could make a significant contribution to advancing the process. “Our most important demand is the freedom and recognition of our leader’s status. author: Unknown
title: Zeynep Karayılan: Peace process cannot be one-sided
content:
Discussions continue over establishing a legal framework for disarmament and the return of members of the Kurdish Freedom Movement as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, launched with the aim of achieving a democratic solution to the Kurdish question. Two years into the process, the National Security Council (MGK) has yet to issue the decision required to implement the framework law passed by parliament on 10 August with the support of 467 MPs.




The law, published in the Official Gazette on 16 August, requires security agencies to verify that disarmament has taken place, with their findings subsequently confirmed by an MGK decision before the mechanism established under the law can be activated. The absence of concrete steps towards implementation, despite parliament beginning its new legislative year and the MGK holding a meeting, has drawn criticism.




Zeynep Karayılan, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), spoke to ANF about the legal dimensions of the process, the shortcomings of the framework law, expectations for democratisation and the steps that need to be taken.







 







‘Implementation of the law requires an MGK decision’

author: Unknown
title: Resistance against solar power project in Amed: “We will not give up our land”
content:
In the village of Arzoxlî (Turkish: Kervanpınar), in the Sur district of Amed (Diyarbakır), resistance against two planned solar power plants continues. For around a week, villagers have been maintaining a vigil in tents on the proposed project site to prevent the destruction of their communal grazing lands. Women are at the forefront of the resistance, fearing for their livelihoods and determined not to surrender the land to the energy company.




The company Zenkar plans to build two photovoltaic facilities, ZENKAR-1 and ZENKAR-2, with associated energy storage systems in Arzoxlî. The projects cover areas of approximately 22.7 and 31.3 hectares, respectively. They are designed to have a combined electricity generation capacity of 33 megawatts and an energy storage capacity of 33 megawatt-hours. The affected areas include communal grazing lands used by villagers who depend primarily on livestock farming, as well as sites of historical and cultural heritage.




Expert report raises doubts about environmental compatibility




A lawsuit challenging the positive environmental impact assessment decision for ZENKAR-2 has been filed with the Administrative Court in Amed. Following a site inspection on July 16, experts concluded that the project’s impact on agriculture, livestock farming, water resources, residential areas, and cultural heritage had not been adequately assessed. title: People’s Initiative in Qamishlo condemns attacks on returnees in Girê Spî
content:
The People’s Initiative of Qamishlo condemned attacks on people who have returned to their home region of Girê Spî (Tal Abyad). At a rally in Martyrs’ Square in Qamishlo, participants called for independent investigations into the attacks and effective protection measures for returnees.




The statement was read out by Wasil Esed, a member of the People’s Initiative, before several dozen people. The initiative demanded comprehensive, transparent, and independent investigations into all human rights violations in Raqqa and Girê Spî: "The circumstances surrounding these violations must be clarified, those responsible identified, and everyone proven to have been involved in the crimes held accountable. At the same time, immediate security measures are needed to protect people returning to their areas of origin."




Call for Kurdish-Arab solidarity




Hassan Farhan Abdulrahman al-Tay, chairman of the Council of Arab Tay Tribes, also spoke at the rally. He condemned attempts to incite tensions between Syria’s different communities. “Through our presence here, we are showing the people of Syria and the international community that we are united. We say no to division and no to those who seek to destroy relations between our peoples,” al-Tay declared.

title: Argentine Human Rights League calls for freedom for Öcalan
content:
The Argentine Human Rights League (Liga Argentina por los Derechos Humanos, LADH) has sent a letter to the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), calling for stronger international efforts to secure the release of Abdullah Öcalan. The organization, itself a member of the federation, also proposes that the FIDH assume a guarantor role in the ongoing peace and democratic society process.




In its letter, the human rights organization, founded in 1937, pointed to the Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 years of imprisonment on the Turkish prison island of Imrali. It said that Öcalan has spent most of this time in solitary confinement and was sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment without any ordinary prospect of release. Even the so-called right to hope—the possibility of having his detention reviewed with a realistic prospect of release—continues to be denied to the Kurdish leader, now 77-year-old, it stated.




“These demands are of crucial importance today”




In its letter, the Human Rights League acknowledges that the FIDH has already addressed Öcalan’s situation on several occasions, recognized him as a political prisoner, and called for his release. However, in light of current political developments, these efforts must be intensified, it noted.

author: Unknown
title: Students in Dêrik demand constitutional recognition of Kurdish
content:
In the city of Dêrik in Rojava, students have once again protested against the education policies of the Syrian transitional government. They are demanding that Kurdish be officially recognized in the Syrian constitution and that the right to education in their mother tongue be guaranteed.




The demonstrators initially gathered outside the school administration building in Dêrik. They then marched to the headquarters of the regional administration, where they met with regional director Şero Şero and presented their demands.




Şero stated that he supported the students’ rights within the framework of a new, democratic Syria. He said the regional administration would forward their demands to the relevant authorities.




The protest concluded with slogans calling for the right to education in the mother tongue and the official recognition of the Kurdish language.

title: Nazan Üstündağ: Democratic integration does not mean being absorbed into the state
content:
According to sociologist Nazan Üstündağ, the democratic integration of Kurdish society must not be confused with adapting to existing state structures. Rather, she says, it involves legally recognizing Kurdish life in its entirety while strengthening society’s independent capacity for political action. Speaking to ANF, Üstündağ emphasized that the development of a democratic society must not wait for state reforms.




The academic made these remarks on the sidelines of a conference on democratic integration organized by Akademî Kurd in Zurich. The concept is one of the central topics of discussion in the ongoing peace and democratic society process. It is closely linked to Abdullah Öcalan’s concept of a democratic society and the question of how relations between the Kurdish population and the Turkish state should be shaped in the future.

Bringing Kurdish life out of illegality




Üstündağ defined democratic integration as both a legal and a social process. title: Students in Rojava oppose the incorporation of their universities into state institutions
content:
The planned incorporation of the universities of Rojava and Kobanê into Syria’s state higher education system has met with resistance from students in Rojava. The Union of Patriotic Students rejects the recent decisions by the Syrian Ministry of Higher Education and warns that they threaten to undermine academic self-governance and Kurdish-language higher education. At a gathering at the University of Rojava in Qamishlo, the organization declared that it would not accept any decision that jeopardizes the educational structures built up over the years or the rights of students.




The dispute stems from two decisions by the Syrian Higher Education Council, announced on October 27. Under these decisions, the University of Rojava in Qamishlo is to be incorporated into the state-run Al-Furat University, while the University of Kobanê is to be placed under the University of Aleppo. Their faculties will henceforth fall under the authority of the respective state universities. Restrictions on the admission of new students are also planned for certain degree programs.




Kurdish-language education under renewed pressure




The decision comes amid growing disputes over the future of the Kurdish-language education system in Rojava. In late August, the Syrian Ministry of Education stipulated that Kurdish would be included in the state curriculum only as a subject taught for three hours

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish athlete arrested after summons in Kermanshah, taken to undisclosed location
content:
Mohammad Nasseri, a Kurdish athlete who manages a bodybuilding gym in Harsin, Kermanshah Province, has been arrested after reporting to a prosecutor’s office in Kermanshah in response to a summons on charges of “propaganda against the state”.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Nasseri was arrested on 26 October after reporting to Branch 16 of the Investigating Office at Kermanshah’s Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office and was taken to an undisclosed location.




He had received the summons in recent days.

title: YJA Star guerrillas: Martyr Bêrîtan is the torch of our struggle
content:
Every year on 25 October, fighters following in the footsteps of Martyr Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş) commemorate the anniversary of her action against the line of betrayal in the free mountains. The date also marks the founding of the women's army. For this reason, guerrillas, particularly women guerrillas, mark the day with great enthusiasm. Guerrillas of the Free Women's Units (YJA Star) shared their feelings on the 34th anniversary of Bêrîtan Hêvî's martyrdom.




YJA Star guerrilla Elefterya Gabar Cizîr began by commemorating Martyr Bêrîtan with respect: “Comrade Bêrîtan became a pioneer and symbol of freedom for us. She understood the reality of Abdullah Öcalan's leadership. She became an example for us and for all women. Comrade Bêrîtan recognised the reality of free women, rebelled against the mentality of betrayal and refused to surrender. Many years may have passed, but she left us a legacy of resistance. That is why we commemorate Comrade Bêrîtan every year. She became a symbol of the will and resistance of free women. Through Martyr Bêrîtan, we came to recognise the will of free women. Through her, we came to understand our own reality. Bêrîtan's personality and action shattered the sexist mentality that underestimated women's strength. This gave us tremendous morale and spiritual strength. Thanks to those martyrs, we came to understand what real life means and the path

title: KRG Interior Ministry opposes Shengal integration, calls for implementation of 9 October Agreement
content:

The Yazidi community welcomed the move, expressing satisfaction that the Iraqi state had recognised Shingal’s defence forces. They also stated that Yazidi rights should be recognised in the Iraqi Constitution in the future.

title: History repeats itself for the Turkish state
content:
The Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has recently been forming a number of alliances. While the AKP and the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) defend these agreements, the opposition has criticised them. Various reasons have been put forward to explain these alliances. However, given that they involve the Middle East and its surrounding region, the first question that comes to mind is their connection to war. Military historians define war as the continuation of politics by other means. From this perspective, it is clear that these alliances risk drawing Turkey into the war in the Middle East.




In fact, the alliance with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan has already drawn Turkey into the war. According to incoming reports and assessments, Turkey has become involved in the ongoing war in Yemen. The Turkish state has sent its armed drones and the specialists who operate them to Saudi Arabia, from where attacks are being carried out against the Houthis in Yemen. As is known, the Houthis are supported by Iran. Turkey has therefore effectively entered into a war with Iran. On the one hand, it claims to oppose the war being waged by the United States and Israel against Iran, while on the other, it is waging war against the Houthis in Yemen.

title: Türkoğlu: We want to speak with disabled women, not for them
content:
The Women's Council and Disability Commission of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), together with Bismil Municipality's Women's Policies Directorate and Disability and Elderly Services Unit, held a meeting with women in Bismil district of Diyarbakır (Amed) under the slogan "Disabled Women Exist Too".




The meeting was attended by DEM Party Women's Council Spokesperson Halide Türkoğlu, Disability Commission Co-Spokesperson Hatice Betül Çelebi and numerous women.







‘Ableist ideology deepens discrimination’




Halide Türkoğlu said at the meeting that disabled women faced inequality and discrimination due to both the male-dominated mentality and ableist ideology. She said that disabled women were being denied the right to make decisions about their own lives and participate in decision-making and governance processes, stressing that their problems and demands must be addressed directly with them.




Türkoğlu said: "We want to speak with disabled women, not on behalf of disabled women," and added that disabled women must be involved in decision-making processes and have control over their own lives. She said that genuine equality could only be achieved by recognising differences, bringing experiences together and leaving no woman behind.

title: The AKP cannot function without war
content:
It is becoming increasingly clear with each passing day that the process initiated by Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan through his February 27, 2025 Call for Peace and Democratic Society amounts, in a sense, to a disruption of the established game. To the domestic and international powers that divided Kurdistan into four parts, imposed genocide on the Kurds, and have benefited from the Kurdish question and the contradictions and conflicts it has generated, the message was effectively: “I will not play the game you want and impose on me. I will play my own game.” In this way, Öcalan has challenged the politics of war and moved toward adopting a politics of peace.




This new strategy and policy developed by Abdullah Öcalan has undoubtedly shocked and bewildered the forces that have tied themselves to, and benefited from, the strategy of conflict arising from the Kurdish question. It appears that the AKP is among those most taken aback. Indeed, under present conditions, when Turkey’s interests and democratic future lie in a politics of peace, the AKP remains unable to break away from its entrenched politics of war and militarization. It has failed to respond positively as required to the peace process initiated by Öcalan. title: DBP and DEM Party: We will be in Varto on 2 November
content:
The Varto (Gimgim) district organizations of the DBP and DEM Party set up a stand in Kox Square as part of the legal proceedings against the geothermal power plant project.




Speaking in a press conference, DBP District Co-Chair Aziz Oral said that the project threatens not only the natural environment but also the living spaces and cultural existence of the local population.




Oral pointed out that potential water pollution could affect agriculture and livestock farming, as well as a wider area of the Euphrates basin via the Murat River. He emphasized the need to protect nature, water resources, and the right of future generations to life.




The DBP and DEM Party called on residents to gather in the village of Xwarik on 2 November for an expert inspection related to the planned geothermal power plant (JES) project in Varto.

author: Unknown
title: Iranian director Jafar Panahi sentenced to 5 years and 1 month in prison
content:
Iranian director and screenwriter Jafar Panahi was sentenced to 5 years and 1 month in prison in a case heard by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The court ordered the confiscation of all his movable and immovable assets, banned him from social media activities for two years, and prohibited him from leaving the country.




According to a report by HRANA, citing Emtedad, Panahi’s lawyer, Mostafa Nili, stated that the verdict had been issued in his client’s absence. Nili said Panahi learned of the ruling after his bank accounts were frozen.




Lawyer Nili said that although his client returned to Iran on March 30, 2026, the case file listed him as being outside the country, and he had not been notified of the hearing date. Nili also stated that an arrest warrant had been issued for Panahi on May 20, 2026, and that the director currently faces three separate legal cases.




Panahi had previously been sentenced to one year in prison in a separate case on charges of “propaganda against the regime.” He was also given a two-year travel ban and prohibited from joining political and social organizations. His request for a retrial was rejected in June 2026.

title: "Women, Justice and Memory" vigil in Amed: “Rojda is not alone”
content:
Women’s organizations have once again protested against patriarchal violence, femicides, and impunity for perpetrators outside the courthouse in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). The “Women, Justice and Memory,” organized by the Network Against Violence, entered its fourth week on Tuesday. Alongside representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, Rojda Odabaşı also took part in today’s demonstration. She had survived an attack in late August when a neighbor shot at her with a shotgun in her apartment.




The participants carried photographs of murdered women and a banner reading “Women hold vigil for justice and memory,” chanting “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî,” “Femicide is political,” and “Long live women’s struggle.”




ÖHD: Rojda’s safety must be ensured immediately




The demonstration focused on demands for protection and justice for Rojda Odabaşı. The suspect had been released late last week following the armed attack on her. Aycan Diril, from the Women’s Commission of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), criticized the decision and called for a thorough investigation into the case. “We demand that Rojda’s safety be ensured immediately, that the decision to release the suspect be subjected to effective judicial review, and that every aspect of the attack, including possible intent to kill, be investigated. title: Trial begins in Leipzig over knife attack on Kurdish woman
content:
Proceedings began today, 27 October, at the Leipzig Regional Court in a case concerning the stabbing and serious injury of a 31-year-old Kurdish woman on a tram on 26 January 2026. The 21-year-old Syrian defendant, Ahmed A., faces charges including aggravated assault, threats, robbery and insult.




According to the indictment, the defendant, Ahmad A., and another person who is being investigated separately insulted and attacked the Kurdish woman aboard tram line 16. The attackers reportedly threatened Kurds, saying, “We will kill all Kurds.”




During the incident, the woman was injured by knife blows and her thumb was severed. It was later surgically reattached at a hospital. She reportedly sustained permanent restrictions in movement and loss of sensation in her hands and fingers, and continues to receive psychological treatment.




Defendant denies anti-Kurdish motive




Speaking in court, the defendant, Ahmed A., admitted to attacking and robbing the victim but claimed that he had no personal issue with Kurds or with the woman he attacked. He said he had consumed alcohol on the night of the incident and had become involved in a knife fight on the tram.




The victim previously told the German newspaper 

Taz

title: At least 87 people executed in Iran in 20 days
content:
The wave of executions in Iran continues. According to the “No Execution Tuesdays” campaign, at least 87 people have been executed in just 20 days. Death sentences have also reportedly been handed down to numerous other prisoners. The protest movement, which has been campaigning against the death penalty and the Iranian regime’s execution practices for more than two and a half years, is now continuing its actions in 66 prisons. On Tuesday, the campaign entered its 144th week.




In a statement, participants warned of the scale of state repression as hundreds, possibly even thousands, of prisoners in Iran are awaiting execution. “The regime uses the death penalty not only to kill people but also to spread fear throughout society and silence opposition voices. Each execution also leaves families in deep grief.”




The campaign highlighted the large number of executions carried out during the Iranian month of Mehr, which lasted from September 22 to October 19. According to the campaign, this development demonstrates how systematically the regime uses the death penalty as a tool of intimidation. “Yet history has shown that no gallows can tear the desire for freedom and equality from people’s hearts. No repression can silence forever the voices of those who fight for their rights,” the statement said.

author: Unknown
title: Convicted rapist Musa Orhan acquitted of charge of inciting suicide
content:
Turkish former non-commissioned officer Musa Orhan, who was sentenced to ten years in prison for raping 18-year-old Kurdish woman İpek Er, has been acquitted in a separate criminal case. On October 22, a court in Batman ruled that it could not be proven that Orhan had incited the young woman to take her own life. The acquittal came despite her suicide note, incriminating witness testimony, and his previous conviction for serious sexual violence. Orhan remains free and has yet to begin serving his prison sentence.




The case of İpek Er sparked outrage far beyond Kurdistan in 2020 and became a symbol of impunity for sexual violence committed by uniformed state personnel. Women’s organizations and the Kurdish women’s movement protested against Orhan’s repeated release from custody and the Turkish judiciary’s handling of the young woman’s case. Even his subsequent conviction did not change the fact that the former soldier remained free.













İpek Er reported being held captive and raped




İpek Er had met Musa Orhan online. In the suicide note she later left behind, she described how the professional soldier, who was stationed in the district of Beşiri at the time, had held her captive for several days, drugged her, and raped her. author: Unknown
title: Swedish Social Democratic Party seeks to strengthen cooperation with DEM Party
content:
Following the confirmation of the Swedish election results, DEM Party co-chairs Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan sent a congratulatory message to Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson.




Magdalena Andersson, who is currently working to form a government in her country, sent a letter addressed to the DEM Party co-chairs.




The letter, shared by the DEM Party Press Office, reads as follows:




“Thank you for your letter and congratulations on behalf of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party. The election results were very close, and this period requires patience, dialogue, and determination. We are doing everything we can to form a government that works for social justice and equal opportunities—ideals that you, too, continue to champion.




At a time of increasing polarization, we must demonstrate that social democracy can deliver results for ordinary people while offering a genuine alternative to the forces seeking to divide us. We deeply value our friendship with the DEM Party. We stand in solidarity with your demands for peace, justice, and democracy in Turkey and look forward to further strengthening our cooperation, both bilaterally and through our shared international platforms.”

author: Unknown
title: Hêzil Özgür: Bêrîtan’s struggle is the story of the free woman
content:
YJAStar (Free Women’s Troops) guerrillas marked the 34th anniversary of the founding of the women’s army with a ceremony and cultural program in the mountains of Kurdistan. The event centered on the legacy of guerrilla commander Bêrîtan Hêvî (Gülnaz Karataş), who fell on October 25, 1992, during the Southern War. Her resistance against surrender and the attacks on the PKK at the time became a defining reference point in the development of an autonomous women’s military organization within the Kurdish freedom movement.




The event began with a speech by Hêzil Özgür from the YJA Star Central Headquarters. Other women guerrilla fighters reflected on Bêrîtan Hêvî’s significance for the women’s freedom movement and the development of a collective identity. The commemoration featured cultural performances and concluded with group dances.




“The women’s army was founded on Bêrîtan’s legacy”




Hêzil Özgür began by recalling the difficult years of 1991 and 1992, when the Kurdish freedom movement was experiencing growing support while simultaneously facing massive military attacks. Particularly large numbers of young women joined the guerrilla forces during this period, she noted. “In those years, participation increased across all sections of society, and the number of female comrades in particular grew significantly. The guerrilla’s influence in Kurdistan grew stronger by the day

author: Unknown
title: Altun: Government must end delaying release of prisoners
content:
Kenan Altun, who had been imprisoned for 30 years, was released from Maltepe No. 1 L-Type Prison in recent days. Altun spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying it had generated great enthusiasm among the people and that prisoners had also strongly embraced the process.




Altun said the Kurdish people had embraced the process, but certain approaches adopted by the government were raising concerns. He added that the situation in prisons was deepening these concerns, pointing to the importance of prison conditions for the progress of the process.







 







‘Prison practices are raising concerns about the process’




Altun drew attention to practices in prisons and said: “It is genuinely difficult to make sense of these practices and explain them to our people. The situation of our imprisoned comrades who have spent many years behind bars, particularly our elderly comrades, is deeply troubling for all of us. One example is Ali Rıza Yurtdaş, who was held in the prison I have just left. He is 84 years old. Despite being referred to the Forensic Medicine Institute several times during this process and having medical reports, he was arbitrarily declared ‘fit to remain in prison’. This is just one example. There are many others.




Apart from our ill comrades, there are prisoners who have served five, ten and even more than thirty years. Their releas

author: Unknown
title: Journalists call for united struggle against repression
content:
Censorship, access restrictions and repressive policies targeting the press and media workers are intensifying, but journalists continue their struggle for a free press in the face of these obstacles. As the public's right to information comes under attack, growing pressure on journalists is deepening restrictions on freedom of expression and press freedom. Free press workers, however, continue to resist these pressures and bring the truth to the public.




Evrensel newspaper reporter Elif Ekin Saltık and Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) Co-Chair Selman Çiçek spoke to ANF about the mounting pressure on the media. They said the repression affects not only journalists but also democratic politics, freedom of expression and the public's right to information. The journalists pointed out that the longstanding repression of the Kurdish press has now expanded to include other opposition media outlets. They called for solidarity and a united struggle against the obstacles facing free and multilingual journalism.




‘The attacks initially targeted the Kurdish press’




Evrensel newspaper reporter Elif Ekin Saltık said that repression in the media had continued for many years, initially targeting the Kurdish press and the Free Press. Saltık said that all opposition groups were now facing similar measures and that the struggle for press freedom could not be separated from the

author: Unknown
title: MSD condemns the attack in Gire Spi: Return of IDPs is an inherent right
content:
The Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) strongly condemned the recent attacks against forcibly displaced Kurdish families returning to Tal Abyad (Gire Spi) in the Raqqa countryside. Returning civilians—including women and children—faced death threats, physical assaults, and property destruction. These violent acts were accompanied by racist slogans targeting Kurdish national identity.




MSD stated that this incident is a grave crime against unarmed civilians, a flagrant violation of the January 29 agreement, and a direct threat to social peace and the right to safe return.




The MSD holds the Syrian Transitional Government fully responsible for protecting civilians, safeguarding their property, and immediately stopping these abuses to prevent their recurrence. It calls for an independent, impartial, and public investigation to reveal the facts, hold both perpetrators and instigators accountable regardless of affiliation, and end systemic impunity. Furthermore, the MSD demands decisive action against hate speech and racial incitement to ensure that no citizen is targeted based on national identity.




The MSD said it is monitoring the rising anger and tension in Hasakah with grave concern, remarking that this public outrage is fully understandable given the severe threats and violations faced by returning families. While calling for restraint and de-escalation to preserve socia

author: Unknown
title: Şener: Flood disasters are not caused by heavy rainfall alone
content:
The floods that followed heavy rainfall in Istanbul last week have once again brought the destruction of the city's ecosystem and unplanned urbanisation into focus. The increasing spread of concrete development, the destruction of natural areas and the disruption of ecological balance are also heightening the risk of disasters.




At least four people lost their lives in the floods. The devastation in Ayazağa, where construction has expanded alongside the destruction of the Northern Forests, has renewed criticism of Istanbul's urban development policies.




Umut Şener from Polen Ecology spoke to ANF about the floods in Istanbul and the consequences of the destruction of the city's ecosystem.




‘The underlying problem is the city's lack of drinking water’




Umut Şener pointed out that ecological destruction in Istanbul has a long history and discussed the environmental problems the city has faced over the centuries.




Şener said, “In the case of Istanbul, it is possible to trace the transformation of nature as far back as antiquity. The environmental problems inherited by the Ottomans when they conquered Istanbul, following centuries of Roman and Byzantine rule, and the measures introduced to address them, demonstrate just how far back this history extends. The decrees concerning ecological matters issued during the Ottoman period, beginning with Sultan Mehmed the Conque

author: Unknown
title: PJAK spokesperson Awdanan: Region preparing for new phase of war
content:
Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) spokesperson Rêwar Awdanan commented on the course of the war between Iran, the US and Israel, as well as developments across the region.




PJAK spokesperson Rêwar Awdanan noted that the Islamic Republic of Iran had suffered devastating defeats in the 12-Day War, the 40-Day War and the Strait of Hormuz War. “Despite this, it continues to act stubbornly and ignores the advice of figures such as Karroubi, Khatami, Zarif and Rouhani. They even view agreements such as the Treaty of Turkmenchay as beneficial to the stability of the system. Negotiations and the Islamabad Agreement were not enough to extinguish the flames of war, because the concessions demanded by each side are unacceptable to the other,” he said.




Negotiations failed to prevent war




Stating that all indications point to preparations for a new phase in the US-Israeli war against the Islamic Republic of Iran, Awdanan said: “The Strait of Hormuz War and the naval and air blockade imposed on Iran demonstrate the reality of the full-scale and intense war we are facing. In the phase preceding the conflict, neither the Islamic Republic of Iran was able to impose on the US and Israel the share of power it wanted in the new Middle Eastern political system, security arrangements, and the region’s trade and economic routes, nor did the US and Israel succeed in bringing the regime under

author: Unknown
title: Seventh denial of release for Nedime Yaklav
content:
In the fourth week of its ongoing protests against the blocking of women prisoners’ releases at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, the Ankara Democratic Institutions Platform made a statement in front of the Ministry of Justice. The protest highlighted the seventh denial of release for Nedime Yaklav, who has been imprisoned for 34 years.




Speaking on behalf of the platform, Nesil Çifçi stated that although there were insufficient social and sporting activities available in the prison, Nedime Yaklav’s failure to participate in these activities had been cited as grounds for denying her release. “Postponing prisoners’ freedom on the basis of facilities that the institution itself fails to provide is not justice; it is oppression,” she said.




Nesil Çifçi stated that, according to data from the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD), the release of 90 prisoners had been blocked over the past three months. She called for an end to the arbitrary obstruction of prisoners who have become eligible for release and demanded that sentence enforcement practices be revised in accordance with human rights principles.




Mehmet Sıddık Akın, Co-Chair of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), also drew attention to violations of the right to health in prisons. He called for the release of seriously ill prisoners, for reports from independent healthcare institutions to be taken into

author: Unknown
title: Bakırhan: 'Peace and Politicisation Council’ must be established immediately
content:
With Abdullah Öcalan’s “Call for Peace and a Democratic Society”, the process entered a new phase. The Kurdish Freedom Movement announced its decision to dissolve itself, burned its weapons and withdrew its forces. However, the state’s delays in taking legal and political steps in response to these moves have increased questions and concerns about the future of the process.




Speaking to ANF, DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan said that trust must be established for the process to move forward and called on the government to take concrete steps. He stressed that the verification and assessment report must be published without delay, that the National Security Council (MGK) must adopt a decision, and that implementation of the Framework Law must begin. “Now it is the government’s turn,” he said.




At last week’s parliamentary group meeting, you pointed out that the government was ‘coming up with a new condition every week and a new pretext every month’. Why is the government dragging its feet? What arguments is it putting forward at the moment?




The way to build trust and establish a future through the “Peace and Democratic Society Process” is for both sides to take reciprocal steps. From Mr Öcalan’s call to the statement issued by the Movement’s Leadership on 8 October, very important steps have been taken since the process began. In response, significant steps were also

author: Unknown
title: Besê Hozat: Abdullah Öcalan’s status must be formalized for the process to move forward
content:
KCK Executive Council Co-Chair Besê Hozat spoke to Medya Haber TV about the current stage of the process, the women’s freedom struggle, practices in prisons, and regional developments.




This is part one of the interview. 




25 October marked the 34th anniversary of the martyrdom of comrade Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), who played a pivotal role in the development of the Kurdish freedom struggle and particularly the women’s resistance movement. What impact did the change she pioneered have on Kurdish sociology?




To begin with, I commemorate all the martyrs of the revolution and the struggle for freedom represented by comrade Bêrîtan with respect, love, and gratitude. Comrade Bêrîtan holds a special place in our struggle. Her place and importance are particularly unique from the perspective of the women’s freedom struggle. Comrade Bêrîtan is a symbol of resistance and of the struggle for freedom. Comrade Bêrîtan’s stance, character, and her resistance – the noble stance she took against the impositions of collaborationists, traitors, and capitulationists, as well as against the line of surrender – have had a tremendous impact on organizing women and on the development of women’s self-defense. Her influence on Kurdish women, in particular, has been immense.




There is a deep-rooted culture of resistance in Kurdistan. Kurdish women play a decisive role in the development and

author: Unknown
title: HPG and YJA-Star guerrillas: Bêrîtan embodies the truth of struggle
content:
People's Defence Forces (HPG) and Free Women's Units (YJA-Star) guerrillas commemorated commander Bêrîtan Hêvî (Gülnaz Karataş) on the anniversary of her martyrdom.




YJA-Star guerrilla Agirî Efrîn spoke about Bêrîtan Hêvî's martyrdom, saying: “I was inspired by comrade Bêrîtan, and it was on this basis that I joined the movement. Today marks the 34th anniversary of her martyrdom. Comrade Bêrîtan was a commander of the women's army, and Abdullah Öcalan developed the women's military organisation following her martyrdom. Her personality is like a light for us women. I had the opportunity to visit the Martyr Bêrîtan Academy myself, which was a great privilege. As a woman, comrade Bêrîtan showed me the right path. She understood Abdullah Öcalan and put his ideas into practice, and for this we owe her a great deal.







 







Comrade Bêrîtan made history through her resistance against the occupiers. No one would knowingly throw themselves off a cliff, but comrade Bêrîtan did so for a cause. In a short period of time, she had embraced and embodied the idea of the free woman. The position of women in society and within the party is different, and we can see this very clearly. The women's army belongs to all women. Women from every nation have a place in our military organisation. Every woman who recognises the importance of her freedom joins the ranks of the women's army. author: Unknown
title: Two Kurdish women missing after being detained
content:
The Voice of Iranian Prisoners Organisation issued a statement concerning two Kurdish women detained in Rojhilatê Kurdistan (East Kurdistan).




The statement said that 17-year-old Perya Nasirî was detained by Iranian intelligence forces at her school in Nexede on 21 October. Six days after her disappearance, her fate and whereabouts remained unknown.




It also stated that Sedrî Bexşî, 43, from the village of Weştape in Bokan, had been held at the Urmiye Intelligence Directorate since her detention a month earlier and was facing serious security-related threats.




After being detained over posts shared on digital media platforms, Sedrî Bexşî had been allowed only one brief telephone conversation with her family, according to the statement. Iranian intelligence forces reportedly threatened the family with severe punishment if they publicised her detention in the media.




According to the report, Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces raided Sedrî Bexşî’s home in the village of Weştape a month ago, using eight armoured vehicles. Following a search of the house, they seized her phone.

author: Unknown
title: Families in Washokani Camp stage protest: We want to return to our homes before winter
content:
Families who were forcibly displaced from Serêkaniyê and Til Temir and are living in Washokani Camp staged a protest today. Blocking the Til Temir–Hesekê road, the families demanded to return to their homes as soon as possible.




The protesters stated that they were facing numerous difficulties in the camp and that no organization was providing them with assistance anymore.




Camp resident Mûsa Mihemed from the village of El Menacîr, said that no organization was helping them anymore and that their living conditions were poor. He explained that winter was approaching and that when it rained, water poured through their torn tents, leaving them exposed to the rain. He demanded that they be enabled to return to their homes as soon as possible.




Another resident of the camp, Cabir Ebdulrehman, said: “I am from the village of El Kêf in Til Temir. We are organizing protests because we want to return to our homes as soon as possible. Our situation is difficult, theft has increased, there is chaos, and we have no means of making a living. We want the return convoys to include all displaced people.”




Mihemed Ebdulrehman, from the village of El Kinêhir in Til Temir, stated: “The return convoys only include people from certain areas. We want to return to our village before winter arrives.”

title: 25 organizations in Europe seek to strengthen joint struggle and solidarity
content:
25 political and civil society organizations from Turkey and Kurdistan have agreed to establish a joint alliance for struggle and solidarity in Europe. The initiative aims to bring together different political currents and strengthen resistance against the rise of right-wing and fascist forces, imperialist war policies, and state repression. At the same time, the participating organizations intend to support the peace and democratic society process in Turkey and advocate for a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.




The agreement stems from a meeting held on October 17 at the Cologne headquarters of the Federation of Alevi Communities in Europe (AABK). Representatives from various political traditions and social movements gathered at the invitation of eight organizations. In a joint final declaration issued today, the participants reaffirm their determination to preserve their organizational independence while establishing a lasting foundation for joint political action.




Against militarism, fascism and imperialist war policies




In their declaration, the organizations describe a world marked by growing international tensions. They warn that wars and conflicts driven by imperialist centers of power are increasing the risk of a broader military confrontation, potentially escalating into a new global war over the redistribution of power and resources. title: Panel discussion on Jineolojî and self-defense in Marseille
content:
A panel discussion and commemoration event focusing on Jineolojî and the formation of women’s armed forces was held in Marseille, France, organized by the Association of Martyrs’ Families (KOMAW), the Marseille Arîn Mîrkan Women’s Council, and members of Jineolojî Provence. The event, held at the Marseille Kurdish Democratic Community Center, was attended by numerous Kurdish women from the region, as well as representatives of French internationalist women’s movements.




The event began with a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the Kurdistan freedom struggle, represented by Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş), described as an immortal commander of the Kurdish women’s struggle, as well as international women revolutionaries who lost their lives defending life.




This was followed by a video presentation highlighting Bêrîtan’s commitment to the principles of women’s freedom and the resistance of Kurdish women in their struggle for liberation. During the screening, chants of “Şehîd namirin” (“Martyrs are immortal) frequently echoed through the hall.

title: Girê Spî Committee calls for the protection of families trapped in Regional Directorate building
content:
A group of Kurdish residents from Girê Spî, who were returning to their homes at the invitation of the Girê Spî Regional Directorate, were attacked while entering the building earlier today.




The Girê Spî Committee for the Forcibly Displaced reported that more than 100 Kurdish families were under siege inside the Regional Directorate building.




The committee described the attack against Kurds as an assault on their safety and their legitimate right to return. It called for the protection of the families and for an immediate investigation into those responsible.




The committee stated that it had been coordinating with relevant parties and following up on efforts to enable forcibly displaced families to return to their homes and properties. These efforts have so far yielded no results, it added.




The committee emphasized that the Regional Directorate officials must fulfill their responsibilities to protect the residents against such attacks.




Drawing attention to the plight of more than 100 Kurdish families, including women and children, trapped inside the Girê Spî Regional Directorate building, the committee called on the relevant authorities to intervene immediately to protect the residents from further attacks.




The committee stated that anyone wishing to return to Girê Spî should contact and coordinate with the committee so that their return can be organized

title: Temelli: Steps toward democratizing the Republic must not be delayed
content:
At a press conference held in Parliament, DEM Party Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Sezai Temelli addressed the peace and democratic society process. He called for the opportunity presented by the process to be seized and for the necessary steps to be taken without delay.




“The democratic resolution to the Kurdish question is the most important step toward comprehensive democratization and the democratization of the Republic,” Temelli said.




Temelli pointed out that the Kurdish question has remained unresolved throughout the Republic’s 100-year history, and that its democratic resolution is of critical importance for the democratization of the Republic.




He emphasized the need to guarantee freedom of the press and expression, protect human rights, and end political bans.




Drawing attention to the continued imprisonment of political figures in Turkey, Temelli cited Figen Yüksekdağ and Selahattin Demirtaş, who are imprisoned in connection with the Kobanê trial, as well as Can Atalay.




Criticizing the Turkish state’s failure to implement rulings of the European Court of Human Rights, Temelli stated that the Republic must embrace democracy and freedoms.

content:

title: YBŞ and YJŞ: Success of the agreement depends on protecting Yazidi rights
content:
The Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ) have confirmed their agreement with the Iraqi government to integrate a total of 4,165 fighters into the state security forces. At a ceremony in the Shengal Mountains on Monday, the two forces stated that the success of the agreement would depend on whether the rights of the Yazidi population were protected, the consequences of the genocide were addressed, and the agreed commitments were fulfilled.




Alongside YBŞ and YJŞ fighters and commanders, the ceremony was attended by Iraq’s Deputy Prime Minister, the Governor of Mosul, representatives of the Iraqi security authorities, as well as Yazidi mothers and religious dignitaries.

content:

content:

title: Özcan Yaman: No liberties, democracy or peace without free media
content:
Journalists took to the streets in several cities on Saturday, 24 October, to protest against the detention and imprisonment of journalists, the appointment of trustees to media outlets and access restrictions imposed on news websites and social media accounts.




The protests were organised following calls by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG), the Mesopotamia Women Journalists Association, the Journalists' Union of Turkey (TGS), the Journalists Association of Turkey (TGC), the Press Council, the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey Press Workers' Union (DISK Basın-Iş), Haber-Sen and the Contemporary Journalists Association (ÇGD). Protesters demanded the release of imprisoned journalists and an end to interference with press freedom.




Journalists and members of the public gathered in front of the Bull Statue in Kadıköy, Istanbul, before marching to Kadıköy Pier Square, chanting slogans. They demanded the release of their colleagues, an end to the appointment of trustees and guarantees for the public's right to information.




ANF spoke to journalists who took to the streets against censorship about the attacks on press freedom and their ongoing struggle.

title: Sevda Karaca: War policies undermine unity and labour struggles - Part Three
content:
Sevda Karaca, Deputy Chair of the Labour Party (EMEP) and MP for Antep, answered ANF's questions about labour struggles and the struggle for peace.




Part one of this interview can be read 

here

here

How do war policies undermine class solidarity between Turkish and Kurdish workers? You frequently visit workplaces and meet workers. Have you observed this in practice?




One of the most important realities we observe on the ground is that workers face very similar economic problems. Workers in Antep, Başpınar, metal factories and the logistics sector talk about inadequate wages, long working hours, workplace accidents, job insecurity and obstacles to trade union organising. Workers living in different cities and belonging to different identities share many of the same problems. But the existence of common problems does not automatically lead to a common struggle.




That requires organisation, trust and shared experiences. War policies and nationalist polarisation undermine precisely these foundations. The conflict of interests between workers and their employers is pushed into the background. Instead of being seen as a fellow worker demanding the same rights, another worker may be portrayed primarily as a representative of a particular identity.
